title: Statistical Analysis Plan for Injury Prediction Models in the MP3 Study
author: Daniel I Rhon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bihfkb3n
materials: Framework: Development of a multivariable prediction model
US active duty military service member.
Service members pending a Medical Evaluation Board.
Statistical Software: The computer software programs R and Python will be used for all analyses.

steps.title: Screen and Enroll Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit US active duty military service members aged 18–45 who were primarily seeking care for a lower extremity or lumbar/thoracic spine injury and are deemed ready to return to work without limitations.

substeps.instruction: Exclude members planning to leave the military within 12 months (separation, retirement, or medical board).
Exclude members with concomitant injuries currently seeking/planning medical care.
Exclude members on restricted or modified work programs due to MSK injury.
Exclude members pending a Medical Evaluation Board.
Exclude members with trauma/polytrauma resulting in amputation.
Exclude members with injuries from high-velocity incidents (e.g., motor vehicle injury).
Exclude members who are pregnant or were pregnant within the last 6 months; withdraw any subject who becomes pregnant during the study.

steps.title: Extract Outcome Data
steps.instruction: Perform a batch extraction of injury data from electronic databases more than 90 days after the last individual completes their 1-year surveillance period.

substeps.instruction: Set date/time parameters to cover the entire 1-year surveillance period (from day of enrollment through the following 364 days).
Extract injury occurrence, type of injury, and number of work-loss days.

steps.title: Clean and Prepare Data
steps.instruction: Process the dataset to ensure eligibility and handle missing values prior to analysis.

substeps.instruction: Remove participants who withdrew consent or were found ineligible after healthcare utilization pull (e.g., not fully cleared for duty).
Categorize missing data as missing completely at random, missing at random, or missing not at random.
If missing data < 5%, perform complete case analysis.
If missing data > 5%, perform multiple imputation with a minimum of 20 iterations (increasing proportionally with the percentage of missing data, e.g., 30% missing = 30 imputations).
Mark missing outcomes prior to imputation; impute outcomes but exclude imputed outcomes from final analyses.
Exclude data categorized as 'missing not at random' from multiple imputation.

steps.title: Perform Preliminary Variable Analysis
steps.instruction: Describe participant characteristics and assess continuous variables for non-linearity.

substeps.instruction: Summarize baseline characteristics (age, sex, BMI, ethnicity, marital status, military rank, years in military, smoking, activity level, and injury category) using mean (SD) for normal distributions, median (IQR) for non-normal distributions, and frequencies/percentages for categorical variables.
Assess continuous variables for non-linearity in relation to injury using restricted cubic splines at three, four, and five knots.
Determine non-linearity based on Akaike’s Information Criteria (AIC), residuals, visual inspection, and biological plausibility.

steps.title: Develop Primary Prediction Model
steps.instruction: Develop a multivariable prediction model using logistic regression with the occurrence of a time-loss injury (at least 1 day of restricted duty) as the binary outcome, following TRIPOD criteria.

substeps.instruction: Select predictors based on clinical reasoning, literature review, and collinearity assessment.
Perform elastic net analysis to assess multicollinearity and shrink coefficients to reduce overfitting.
Determine optimal alpha and lambda shrinkage parameters using tenfold cross-validation with ten iterations per fold, selecting based on the greatest Kappa.
Internally validate the model to decrease optimism using either bootstrapping with 2000 iterations or 10-fold cross-validation with 10 iterations per fold.

steps.title: Evaluate Model Performance
steps.instruction: Investigate the performance of the primary model using calibration and discrimination metrics.

substeps.instruction: Quantify calibration using the calibration slope (with 95% confidence intervals) and a loess smoother plot of predicted risk against observed outcome.
Evaluate discrimination using the Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC).
Assess Nagelkerke R-squared.
Report intercept, coefficients, standard errors, 95% confidence intervals, and P values for predictors.

steps.title: Conduct Sensitivity and Subgroup Analyses
steps.instruction: Perform additional logistic regressions to investigate the robustness of the results.

substeps.instruction: Run logistic regression for participants without pain.
Run separate logistic regressions for spine and lower extremity cohorts.
Run logistic regressions for injury severity.
Perform survival analysis in relation to time to injury.

steps.title: Develop Machine Learning Models
steps.instruction: Develop four machine learning models using the same predictors as the logistic regression model: Random Forest, Support Vector Machine Regression, Gradient Boosting Machine, and Artificial Neural Networks.

substeps.instruction: Use an iterative matrix process to assess optimal tuning hyperparameters, utilizing root mean square error (RMSE) to determine optimal tuning.
Internally validate all ML models to reduce overfitting using 10-fold cross-validation.
Determine the importance and weight of predictors.

steps.title: Perform Decision Curve Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct decision curve analyses to determine if the prediction model improves military outcomes compared to 'treat all', 'treat none', and current evidence-based practice guidelines.

substeps.instruction: Define the threshold probability as the population risk of injury within military personnel.
Calculate net benefit across a range of predicted risks.
